RMIT Vietnam

RMIT is a global university of technology, design and enterprise.

As one of Australia's original tertiary institutions with more than 100 years of establishment, RMIT University enjoys an international reputation for excellence in professional and vocational education, applied research, and engagement with the needs of industry and the community.

RMIT Vietnam campus was established in 2000, and brings a world-class education and globalised study environment to one of the fastest growing regions in Asia. RMIT Vietnam offers programs in business, technology, communication, design, fashion, and languages, and boasts an impressive range of extra-curricular activities that encourage students to break new ground in their areas of interest.

As of today, RMIT university has 3 campuses in Melbourne in Australia and 2 campuses in Vietnam (Ho Chi Minh City and the capital city Hanoi). Its HCMC campus has 11,500 students, with 600 international students.
administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Original Epitech Transcripts (translated in English and certified, sent by Epitech)
  • English Language Certificate equivalent to CEFR B2 (will be provided by Epitech)
  • A copy of portrait photo
  • Copy of passport with bio data base


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.

Attention! Tuition fees payment will be sent by Epitech to RMIT.


Please do not settle any tuition fee payment to the host university.


2. Visa (more information here)

You will need to apply for a student visa once you are officially accepted at RMIT Vietnam.

For more information, please refer to the Vietnam Embassy in France (here) or to the visa page on RMIT Vietnam's website (here). The visa should cost you about 90€.


Students may enter Vietnam up to 4 weeks before the semester start date and remain for up to 4 weeks after the course end date. In total, the visa covers approximately 5 months per trimester.


3. Insurance & Health

RMIT University Vietnam will arrange suitable medical insurance on behalf of the student. The insurance fee of $251 (5,700,000 VND) is included in the tuition fee invoice per semester. 


We also highly recommend you to purchase an international insurance in France that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.


To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/vietnam

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

To prepare your arrival and read more information about the supports offered to international students, please click here and here.

RMIT Vietnam International Student Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/rmitvnstudentlife


5. Campus Life

Our students will follow courses at the Ho Chi Minh campus. Click on the following links for photos & a virtual tour of the campus.

accomodation:
On-campus accommodation

RMIT Vietnam does not have on-campus housing.


Off-campus accommodation (more information here)

RMIT Vietnam provides a range of support services and resources to help you find safe and suitable accommodation near campus. 

Renting serviced and furnished apartments is far more common in Vietnam than in westernised countries. Don’t worry - we will link you with a Vietnamese student who will become your ‘buddy’ and help you out. The standard of accommodation in Ho Chi Minh is very good with a wide range of guesthouses, houses and apartments catering to all budgets, depending on location, lifestyle and individual circumstances.

Living near the RMIT Saigon South campus also gives you a great opportunity to enjoy cuisines from other countries. This modern residential area is quieter than the city and has a high population of foreigners and a variety of well-priced cafes and restaurants. Of course, the local supermarkets and convenience stores sell everything you need to prepare your own, inexpensive, meals.
courses:
Credits

You should validate 4 courses per trimester, each course worth 12 local credits.

To obtain 60 ECTS for your 4th year, you are required to successfully complete 8 courses and earn 96 local credits by the end of your study with RMIT Vietnam.


Academic Calendar (more information here)

Our students will study 2 trimesters at RMIT Vietnam:

  • October intake: 26 october 2026, with an orientation week starting on the 19h of October
  • January intake

cost:
Financial Overview for Studying at RMIT (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses / Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Vietnamese dong. 1 € = 30 000 VND (rate October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


  • Roundtrip flights: from 1000€
  • Insurance: 250$
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage
  • Visa: 90€
  • Housing: 300-600€
  • Utilities (electricity, water, gas, phone & internet): 50-70€
  • Food: 200-300€ / food in local street food stalls 2-3€ / dining in restaurant 5-10€
  • Transport: 50-70€ /taxi fares are about 0.5€/km. There are also ride-sharing apps like Grab.

These costs are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

Reliable taxi services include Vinasun Taxi, Grab or Mailinh Taxi.

Unit Price: VND 15,000 – 18,000 per km
